E1.evidence: Issue #864 gives a full reproducer (roslaunch rosbridge_websocket, rostopic pub of sensor_msgs/NavSatFix, a Python autobahn client subscribing with 'compression': 'cbor') and the error log: "[MultiSubscriber.callback]: Exception calling subscribe callback: 'float' object has no attribute '__slots__'". Reporter: "Library Version: 0.11.16 - ROS Version: ROS 1 Noetic". https://github.com/RobotWebTools/rosbridge_suite/issues/864

units_identified: sensor_msgs/NavSatFix publisher (rostopic pub) and the CBOR-requesting WebSocket client
E2.evidence: The crash is in rosbridge_library's own CBOR encoder. It matches the genpy slot type string against a fixed table that only lists variable-length array spellings: "TAGGED_ARRAY_FORMATS = { ... 'float32[]': (85, '<{}f'), 'float64[]': (86, '<{}d'), }" (cbor_conversion.py at b0d0d711). A fixed-length field such as NavSatFix.position_covariance has slot type 'float64[9]', which is the correct ROS 1 spelling, so it falls through to the "array of messages" branch "out[slot] = [extract_cbor_values(i) for i in val]" and recurses into floats. Reporter: "in that dict, the syntax supported is only for variable length arrays ... While in this case, the variable `slot_type` has the value: `float64[9]`" and "Replacing `float64[]` by `float64[9]` works but is obviously not generic." Nothing wrong crosses the boundary: the publisher, the message definition and the client request are all correct, and any correct publisher of a message with a fixed-length numeric array (with any correct client requesting cbor) triggers the same crash. This is a missing case in one unit's own serialization logic.

E3.evidence: PAIR: rosbridge subscribes to /nav (published by rostopic pub) and forwards it CBOR-encoded to the WebSocket client; the failure occurs in the subscribe callback.

E4.evidence: Observed failure: "The rosbridge server fails wit the error: [MultiSubscriber.callback]: Exception calling subscribe callback: 'float' object has no attribute '__slots__'".

ineligible_reason: internal: rosbridge_library's CBOR encoder does not recognise fixed-length array slot types (e.g. 'float64[9]') and crashes on any correct message containing one; no mismatched value, name, frame or timing crosses a unit boundary.
notes: The packet's fix reference PR #883 ('Handle ROS 2 types properly', merged 2023-10-27 into ros2 as 910163bd) changes only rosapi/objectutils.py typedef building and does not touch cbor_conversion.py; its body says 'Fixes #834 #822 #821'. Issue #864 was closed by the stale bot as not_planned on 2024-07-31 with no fix. PR #882 (501a926c, ros2 branch) rewrote the table keys to 'sequence<double>' etc., which still would not match a fixed-length ROS 2 array type string such as 'double[9]'; later ros2 commits (97a2434f 'Replace cbor with cbor2 library, remove inline implementation') were not examined because the case stops at E2. Alternative reading considered: the genpy slot-type string crossing from the generated message class into rosbridge could be treated as a representation convention, but the string is correct per the ROS 1 type system and the defect is rosbridge's incomplete handling, so it is classified internal. ROS 1 Noetic, rosbridge 0.11.16; reporter states the ros2 branch has the same issue.
